A.why: Nice moss-banded pale bodice, but the skirt is a front-only apron; back and side read as legs, with no flare.
A.fix: Wrap a flared, overlapping skirt all the way round to the shins and narrow the boxy shoulders.

B.why: A coherent pale/bronze/moss robe with a good crested helm, but a straight column with no waist or flare, and broad square shoulders.
B.fix: Cinch the waist and step the skirt outward in tiers; slim the sleeves; mute the gold visor.

C.why: The most distinctive ruin-stone ziggurat skirt, with clean tiers and a strong top-down read, but the torso, shoulders and crown are blocky and golem-like.
C.fix: Pull in the waist, narrow the shoulders, replace the chimney crown with a wide low circlet, and add moss and bronze tier lips.

D.why: The most feminine and courtly: V-neck cuirass, hooped tassets with bronze cords, moss hem. But the skirt tucks in at the hem and the sleeves are bulky.
D.fix: Make the lowest hoop the widest point at the shins; overlap and thicken the tassets on the slim fit; slim the sleeves.

E.why: Mid-grey with a straight split skirt and big square shoulders; reads as an iron knight in a surcoat, not pale ruinplate.
E.fix: Lift the base colour to pale bone stone, flare the skirt, shrink the shoulders, mute the visor.

F.why: A clear tiered bell gown with bronze lips and moss bands, a fitted waist band, and tiers that hold on the slim avatar. Best overall read.
F.fix: Replace the fist-like prong crest with a clean crown or fan crest; slim the sleeves; age the brightest hem tier toward bone.

notes: The tiered and stepped skirts (F, C) win the high-camera read and feel like Grashan ruin stone. D has the most femininity and elegance and should feed its waist and neckline language into the winner. Nearly every candidate has square, torso-width sleeve and shoulder blocks, which works against the narrow-shoulder brief; that is the common fix. Gold visors read too bright across B, E and F. Recommend keeping F, C and D.
